home-photo.title: photograph
home-photo.alt: Black-and-white landscape with a solitary tree beneath large clouds.

manual-play-prompt.title: layout prompt
manual-play-prompt.body: Feel free to mess up this layout. You can just...

manual-start-a.title: 01 / set up the CDN
manual-start-a.body: Start by loading the latest release. The CDN brings the library's stylesheet and JavaScript module into your page.

manual-start-div.title: div
manual-start-div.body: Add an empty div to your HTML. This is the field where the blocks will appear.

manual-start-blocks.title: blocks
manual-start-blocks.body: Create the system and attach it to that div. From then on, blocks controls the field.

manual-start-grid.title: grid
manual-start-grid.body: Set the field to a 4 × 4 grid before adding content. That gives you four columns and four rows.

manual-finish.title: 02 / content can be anything
manual-finish.statement: A block can hold anything the browser can render.

manual-content-html-intro.title: HTML
manual-content-html-intro.intro: Pass an HTML string to use markup as the block's content.

manual-content-object-intro.title: image
manual-content-object-intro.intro: Use a browser element for text, images, SVG, canvas, forms or media. For untrusted text, set textContent.

manual-content-object.title: result
manual-content-object.alt: Black-and-white skatepark with converging concrete ramps, painted lines and a metal rail.

manual-content-factory-intro.title: interactive
manual-content-factory-intro.intro: Use a function when every added block needs a fresh element and its own interaction.

manual-content-waves-intro.title: library
manual-content-waves-intro.intro: A grid of characters, each glyph chosen from a shifting vanilla.waves sampler. The renderer lives in its own file; this example only sets up the element and adds it as a block.

manual-menu.title: 03 / titlebar controls
manual-menu.intro: Every block starts with minimize and close in its top-right corner. The API calls the titlebar configuration menu. A controller can also minimize, restore or remove its own block. Close removes an example; reset restores the full manual.

manual-menu-minimize.title: restore
manual-menu-minimize.body: Use + to show the content again.

manual-menu-none.title: reset
manual-menu-none.body: Use reset above to restore the lesson.

manual-layout.title: block size and position
manual-layout.intro: Set size first, then position. Columns come before rows and coordinates start at 1.

manual-drag.title: 04 / dragging
manual-drag.intro: Every block moves by its titlebar. Fixed-grid keeps each move on the grid; set draggable false only for a block that must keep its place.

manual-base-colors.title: 05 / set the base colors
manual-base-colors.intro: Set the field, paper, titlebar and text colors once on the container. Every block inherits these four CSS variables unless you override one block later.

manual-appearance.title: 06 / choose an appearance
manual-appearance.intro: Choose one fixed monochrome variant. Regular uses dark ink on paper; inverse exchanges figure and ground. Color and chance come later.

manual-colors.title: 07 / set a color
manual-colors.intro: Set one block color directly. Any valid CSS color fills its titlebar; every block keeps the same thin black border and stronger black hover frame. The content stays neutral unless the block is inverse.

manual-random.title: 08 / set the chance
manual-random.intro: Set both chances between 0 and 1. colorVariation is checked first. inversionVariation applies only to blocks that remain monochrome. The twelve blocks below use the current values.

manual-random-action.title: settings
manual-random-action.intro: Move either slider to update the code and create twelve new blocks. Random chooses a new pair of slider values.

manual-next.title: 09 / unblocked
manual-next.statement: So, the blocks are unblocked now.

reference-system-create.title: create the system
reference-system-create.intro: Import the factory and create one independent blocks system. The module also exports a shared system when one global instance is enough.
code: blockDefaults: { menu: { minimize: true, close: true } },

cells: Create an independent blocks system; the complete options object is shown above.
The same shared instance exposed in a browser.
Base URL used by address() when a block has no url of its own.
Set a family and optional stylesheet URL; blocks.font remains writable.
Partial<{ move, resize, restore, minimize, close }>
Override resolved accessible labels; blocks.labels is readonly.

reference-container.title: attach a container
reference-container.intro: Attach the system to one existing element before adding content. A selector and an Element are both accepted.

cells: Attach to a selector or Element.

reference-grid.title: set the grid
reference-grid.intro: Choose one layout when creating the system. Fixed-grid uses explicit addresses; flow-grid uses DOM order and only each block's starting size.

cells: Current column count; starts at 1 and changes through setGrid().
Current row count; starts at 1 and may also grow after dragging.
One complete layout model chosen at creation; it cannot change afterwards.
Move fixed grid blocks upward to fill vertical gaps.

reference-block-create.title: create a block
reference-block-create.intro: add() turns content into one block and returns its controller. id identifies the block; title is optional visible text in its titlebar.

cells: Add content and return one BlockController; every option is shown above.
Optional visible titlebar text. Without it, id remains only the accessible fallback for actions.
Configure titlebar controls for this block.
Override the system appearance for this block.
Allow this block to move while the system remains draggable.

reference-block-layout.title: size and position
reference-block-layout.intro: Set a block span in whole grid units. Fixed-grid also accepts coordinates; flow-grid always follows DOM order and automatically shifts later blocks.

cells: Set the size in whole grid units.
Set one-based coordinates in fixed-grid; other modes reject the call.
Export the mode, content-free DOM order and each block's span, place and minimized state.
Restore a matching version 1 layout; another mode is rejected, unknown ids are ignored and unsaved blocks follow the saved ones.
Resize event sizes use positive whole grid units.

reference-block-layout.details: In flow-grid, add blocks in the desired initial order—for example after sorting titles by name—and call span() without place().

reference-content.title: choose the content
reference-content.intro: A block accepts trusted HTML, a Node or a factory. Never pass untrusted text as HTML; create an element and assign textContent instead.

cells: Trusted markup parsed by the browser.
An existing DOM node; use textContent here for untrusted text.
Create fresh content when add() runs.
The content host inside the returned block.

reference-titlebar.title: titlebar controls
reference-titlebar.intro: Configure minimize and close when the system or block is created, or update one block later through its controller. Fixed-grid keeps a minimized block's assigned footprint; flow-grid reduces it to one titlebar row without changing DOM order.

cells: Default titlebar controls for new blocks; minimize and close are both enabled initially.
Enable, disable or configure controls for one new block.
Read or change the current minimized state.
Add or update the titlebar; options accepts minimize and close.
Remove the block. Fixed-grid leaves its address empty until an explicit compact(); flow-grid closes the gap automatically through DOM order.

reference-dragging.title: dragging and order
reference-dragging.intro: draggable enables pointer and keyboard movement. Fixed-grid moves coordinates; free and flow-grid change DOM order. Optional resize lines change every non-minimized flow-grid block's span.

cells: Allow pointer and keyboard reordering for the whole system.
Set the initial drag state for one new block.
Read or change whether one block can move.
Enable resize lines in flow-grid; other layouts reject true.
Fires after a pointer or keyboard move.
Fires with id, input, axis, from and to after a pointer or keyboard resize.

reference-dragging.details: input is pointer or keyboard; mode is grid or flow; from and to are { column, row } or null. direction is up, right, down, left or still.

reference-appearance.title: choose an appearance
reference-appearance.intro: Set a default appearance for future blocks or override it on one block. Built-in fixed variants are regular and inverse; random delegates to the chance settings.

cells: Read or change the default appearance.
The built-in fixed list: regular and inverse.
Override the system appearance for one new block.
Read or change the resolved appearance of one block.

reference-color.title: set a color
reference-color.intro: Assign one CSS color directly to a block, or provide an array used by future random blocks.

cells: User-owned CSS colors available to future random blocks.
Read or replace the current color source.
Read or set one block's CSS color.

reference-chance.title: set the chance
reference-chance.intro: Chance only affects future blocks created with the random variant. Color is checked first; inversion applies to the remaining monochrome blocks.

cells: Random source used for appearance decisions.
Share from 0 to 1 that uses colorArray; a positive value needs colors.
Inverse share from 0 to 1 inside the remaining monochrome range.

reference-block-controller.title: inspect and serialize a block
reference-block-controller.intro: add() returns one controller. Use it instead of removing or rewriting the outer DOM element directly.

cells: The outer block element. Do not call element.remove(); use remove() so the system releases its layout.
The content host inside the block.
Read or change whether this block can move.
Serialize this live block for the built-in html adapter.
Name the page in the serialized definition.
Build ?block=id from definition.url or the system catalogUrl.

reference-definition-create.title: definitions + adapters
reference-definition-create.intro: Definitions describe reusable content. Register definitions and their lifecycle adapters on the shared system.

cells: Replace an existing definition or adapter deliberately.
Page the block lives on; address() prefers it over the catalogUrl.
Content used by the built-in html adapter.
Mounts and snippets trusted definition.markup. Replace it with registerAdapter("html", adapter, { replace: true }).
List registered adapter ids, starting with the built-in html adapter.
Filter definitions with any combination of the four filters below.
Match text in the definition id, label, description, adapter, medium or category.
Keep definitions that use this adapter id.

reference-adapter-methods.title: adapter lifecycle methods
reference-adapter-methods.intro: Adapters own mount and cleanup lifecycle; the system methods below use those lifecycle hooks for registered definitions.

cells: Mount a registered definition through its adapter.
Run optional cleanup and remove mounted content.
Unmount and mount again with new settings.
Ask the adapter for a reusable snippet.
Adapter-specific settings merged over definition.defaults; for the note adapter, { text: "hello" } is valid.
Return the direct child root Element or { node }, directly or through a Promise. Context contains block, host, settings and adapter.
Prepare before mount with the same context as mount.
Release listeners or resources. Mounted contains the mount context plus node.
Receives block and settings only; return reusable source text.
The node returned by mount and tracked for cleanup.

reference-field-signals.title: field events + DOM hooks
reference-field-signals.intro: The attached field exposes stable DOM hooks and dispatches state, reorder and resize events.
reference-field-signals.details: For blocks:change, type is compact, minimize, restore or remove; id is one block or null, and ids lists affected blocks.

cells: Fires after an explicit compact, minimize, restore or remove state change.
Fires after pointer or keyboard resizing with id, input, axis, from and to.
The attached field and its layout tokens.
Structural title bar and pointer drag area.
Keyboard drag handle with button semantics while dragging is enabled.
Resolved appearance. Custom variant names pass validation and land here for consumer styling — for example a light footnote weight.
Color selected from the user's array.
The single free, fixed-grid or flow-grid layout mode.
Effective resize state for one block.
Effective drag state for one block.

reference-system-errors.title: failures + boundaries
reference-system-errors.details: Expect errors for invalid or duplicate ids, missing fields, impossible grid positions, overlaps, unknown definitions, incomplete adapters and colorVariation without colors. Catch only errors your interface can recover from.
